full-pool diversity is key; trimmed mean adds robustness to worst models without losing cross-family signal
unstable ranking across windows suggests per-horizon top-k selection adapts better than a fixed pool; k=3 keeps diversity while focusing on locally best models
pruned pool keeps one representative per correlated-error group, maximizing family diversity; mean is robust to unstable ranking

decision.justification: The series is seasonal-dominated (strength 0.99) with unstable model ranking (Kendall tau -0.22) and high cross-model error correlation (mean 0.88). Pool4 retains one representative per correlated-error group (ETS for the ARIMA/ETS/THETA family, catboost for the ML family, NaiveSeasonal for pure seasonal capture, NaiveMovingAverage for level tracking), maximizing family diversity. A simple mean over these diverse representatives is robust to the unstable ranking and avoids amplifying correlated errors, which is exactly what the series profile calls for. The separated margin over the runner-up confirms this is a genuine improvement, not noise.
